subject.title: [Feature]: Webhook hook sessions should reuse existing session when sessionKey is consistent (multi-turn support)

question: Should authenticated hook callers be allowed to opt into re-entering an existing session when their supplied or templated session key passes the configured request-key and prefix policy?
rationale: Persistent mode intentionally selects stored transcript and runtime context, while the session key is routing context rather than an independent authentication boundary; maintainers must confirm which callers may inherit that state.

options.title: Allow Explicit Persistence
options.body: Permit sessionMode="persistent" only for authenticated hooks whose keys pass allowRequestSessionKey and allowedSessionKeyPrefixes policy, while keeping isolated as the default.

options.title: Keep Hooks Isolated
options.body: Reject stored-session re-entry and revise the hook documentation to state that stable keys provide routing and metadata continuity only.

options.title: Create Separate Session API
options.body: Keep hook-agent isolated and expose trusted existing-session delivery through a distinct API with stronger authorization and state controls.

recommendation.title: Allow Explicit Persistence
recommendation.body: Permit sessionMode="persistent" only for authenticated hooks whose keys pass allowRequestSessionKey and allowedSessionKeyPrefixes policy, while keeping isolated as the default.
